name: Mathews' Purple
lede: Mathews' Purple is a mid-toned, reddish purple from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color standards, and no book we hold records whom it honors.

sections.title: A name the books leave open
sections.body:
Ridgway placed this purple on plate XXV of his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, giving it the hue number 65' [1]. Ridgway assembled his roughly 4,000 named samples from many earlier sources rather than coining every name himself, so a color carrying a person's name in his book is not necessarily his own naming [2]. No book we hold explains who Mathews was [1][2].

Its nearest library neighbors are [[razzmic-berry|Purpleish]] and the lighter, bluer [[viola|Dark Lilac]], with the brighter [[viola|Viola]] close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In LCH terms it measures lightness 49, chroma 36, hue 328 degrees, a stronger purple than its nearest archive cousin [[plum]] [3]. Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no match for this purple at our usual threshold [4]. That is common for saturated purples: pigments fade and darken unevenly on aged, varnished canvases, so a close match can simply fall under our five-percent-of-canvas rule [4].

origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature (1912)
